text:
Elaine: Heads-up — sketched a light IA change for the console rail to improve deep-link stability and make breadcrumb behavior more predictable. TL;DR: group nav by workflow (Datasets / Models / Endpoints), breadcrumbs reflect flow, and preserve ?tab= and ?panel= across route rewrites. (Sketch in thread)
Sam: Dropping a quick Figma proto: https://www.figma.com/file/placeholder/rail-ia-proto — it shows grouped sections and a compact accordion for smaller widths.
Priya: Love the grouping idea. Quick worry: top-level rail feels dense on small screens, could be overwhelming.
Matt: Can we auto-collapse groups into an accordion at <= 1200px? Keyboard access must be intact for a11y.
DesignBot: Accessibility nits: when a group expands, move focus to the first link in that group. Add aria-expanded, aria-controls. Add a skip link ("Skip to main") that exposes on keyboard focus. Also ensure focus returns when group collapses. :white_check_mark:
Elaine: Also thinking about deep links shape — we should canonicalize anchors into path segments. e.g. `/orgs/:org/apps/:app#predictions` -> `/orgs/:org/apps/:app/predictions`. Keeps routing consistent.
Sam: That rewrite will break old shared links. Proposal: accept legacy anchors and do a client-side rewrite using history.replaceState to canonical path (no extra history entry) and show a one-time toast when redirecting from an old link. This preserves shareability and avoids back-button surprises.
Priya: How do we treat ephemeral overlays like `/compose`? If they become nested under grouped parents, back/escape behavior gets weird.
Matt: Suggest keeping ephemeral UIs as query params: `?overlay=compose` or `?modal=compose`. That avoids forcing them into the sidebar's nesting model and keeps keyboard ESC semantics predictable.
Elaine: Breadcrumbs: show Workspace > App > Subflow. Question: Do we expose internal IDs in the breadcrumb? Privacy / accidental leak concern for support links.
Priya: Use slugs only (human-readable). Also truncate long breadcrumb trails on mobile and show an overflow menu for older segments.
Sam: Example mapping I'm proposing:
```
/orgs/:orgSlug/apps/:appSlug
/orgs/:orgSlug/apps/:appSlug/predictions
/orgs/:orgSlug/apps/:appSlug/versions/:versionId
```
Client accepts `#predictions` but rewrites to `/predictions`.
Elaine: Important: preserve attribution params like `?from_dashboard=true` when rewriting so analytics attribution doesn't drop off.
Matt: Rollout plan: canary to 10% of orgs. Ops must log oldPath -> newPath mapping for debugging. Also flag regressions for session replay.
Priya: @Sam please add keyboard navigation tests to the rollout checklist: pptr test for focus order, skip link presence, and accordion keyboard controls.
Sam: Will add tests and a checklist entry. Filing ticket: https://linear.app/rw/issue/PROD-rail-ia-2101 (placeholder)
Elaine: Decision for now: implement grouped rail + canonical path rewrites + accordion collapse <= 1200px + a11y focus rules + preserve query params for ephemeral overlays. I'll draft the spec and link it here. :rocket:
Matt: Minor nit — when a user follows a canonicalized link, avoid showing the toast more than once per session. Otherwise it's noisy. :point_up:
DesignBot: Added a11y test checklist to the design spec doc: focus order, aria attributes, skip-link, screenreader announcement after rewrite. :memo:
Sam: Putting PR template together for the change. Will include migration helper and redirect mapping in server logs.
Elaine: Cool — thanks everyone. Next step: design spec + dev RFC + a11y test plan. @Sam can you post the spec link when ready? :thumbsup:
thread_summary: Design thread discussing console rail IA changes: grouping nav by workflow, canonicalizing anchors to path segments, accordion collapse on small screens, preserving query params, accessibility requirements, and canary rollout plan.
